topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture aims, context, and framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth Signaling and Insensitivity to Growth Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and mutations underlying self-sufficient growth signaling and evasion of inhibitory pathways, focusing on Wnt, RTK, and TGF-beta cascades.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation in both hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through alterations in p53 and mitochondrial regulatory proteins like Bax and BCL2.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss telomere biology, telomerase activation, and the normal stress-induced senescence mechanisms mediated by p53.

topics.label: Cancer Metabolism and Rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex cellular phenotypes by examining aerobic glycolysis, the Warburg effect, oncometabolites, and metabolic interactions with the epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the requirement for new blood vessel formation, the timing of the angiogenic switch during tumor progression, and its molecular balance.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the physical and biological processes of tumor dissemination, circulation survival, liquid biopsies, and the genetic features of metastatic disease.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This final subtopic provides concluding remarks on the integration of cancer hallmarks, references recent literature, and closes the lecture.
